title: Row, Row, Row Your Boat
composer: Traditional (American); tune printed with these words in 1881, credited to Eliphalet Oram Lyte
tempo_note: PianoFlow teaching suggestion; Octotune starts it at quarter = 90.
form: A B (4-bar phrases); usually sung as a round
keyboard: Fits the GarageKey Mini range C3–C6 (MIDI 48–84). Melody is C4–C5; left hand stays on or above C3.
setting: PianoFlow teaching setting: verified traditional melody in the right hand, in C; the left-hand roots and blocked C and G chords are written for this catalog, not taken from a source arrangement.
lyric_snippet: Row, row, row your boat, gently down the stream. Merrily, merrily, merrily, merrily, life is but a dream.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Row, Row, Row Your Boat (article and its LilyPond melody)
sources.used_for: Note-level source with rhythm: \time 6/8, c4. c4. | c4 d8 e4. | e4 d8 e4 f8 | g2. | c8 c c g g g | e e e c c c | g'4 f8 e4 d8 | c2. (C4 to C5). History: earliest printing 1852 with a different tune; the modern tune with these words in 1881 (The Franklin Square Song Collection), mentioning Eliphalet Oram Lyte.

sources.title: Trebly, Row, Row, Row Your Boat notes (letter names with beat lengths)
sources.used_for: Independent note-level cross-check: the same 27 notes and beat lengths bar by bar, 8 measures of 6/8 (dotted quarters, quarter-eighth pairs, eighth-note merrilys, dotted halves).

sources.title: Octotune, Row, Row, Row Your Boat easy piano notes
sources.used_for: Pitch and octave cross-check: C4 to C5, C major, 6/8, 8 measures, the same letters bar by bar; it also suggests moving to G position for the merrilys. Its left-hand part was not used.

variants: The modern round tune (1881) is used, not the 1852 or 1854 tunes. All three sources agree on every pitch; Wikipedia and Trebly agree on every duration. Harmony C throughout with G in bar 7 matches ePiano's chord names; the left-hand voicings are this catalog's own (the G chord is D3 G3 B3 to stay at or above C3).

notes.five-finger-position: C position, one finger per key from C up to G; steps only.
notes.one-hand-melody: The 6/8 long-short swing (dotted quarters and quarter-eighth pairs) at a slow two-beat pulse.
notes.hands-together: LH chords land on the two main beats while the RH plays its long-short pairs.
notes.basic-chords: One close C triad, repeated slowly; the hand never changes shape.

ladder.label: Right hand alone
ladder.play: RH, thumb on middle C: C(dotted quarter) C(dotted quarter) | C(quarter) D(eighth) E(dotted quarter) | E(quarter) D(eighth) E(quarter) F(eighth) | G(dotted half). Fingers 1-1 | 1-2-3 | 3-2-3-4 | 5. Two beats a bar, about 60 a minute.

ladder.label: Right hand and left-hand roots
ladder.play: RH as before; LH holds C3 for each bar (dotted half notes).

ladder.label: Both hands (teaching setting)
ladder.play: RH as before; LH plays a C3 E3 G3 chord on each beat (two dotted quarters a bar) in bars 1-3 and holds it through bar 4.

notes.five-finger-position: Each half of the phrase sits in one five-key position.
notes.one-hand-melody: Twelve even eighth notes in groups of three, then the long-short close.
notes.position-shifts: The tune spans an octave (C4-C5): the hand moves up to G position for the high C and back to C position a beat later.
notes.hands-together: LH chords on each beat under the twelve quick RH eighths, including the move between positions.
notes.basic-chords: Close C and G triads, two a bar.
notes.inversions: The G chord is played with D at the bottom (D3 G3 B3), which keeps the left hand at or above C3.

ladder.label: Right hand alone
ladder.play: RH moves up to G position for the merrilys (thumb on G4, finger 4 on C5): C5 C5 C5 G4 G4 G4 (eighths) | then back to C position: E E E C C C (eighths) | G(quarter) F(eighth) E(quarter) D(eighth) | C(dotted half).

ladder.label: Right hand and left-hand roots
ladder.play: RH as before; LH holds C3 (bars 5-6), G3 (bar 7), C3 (bar 8).

ladder.label: Both hands (teaching setting)
ladder.play: RH as before; LH plays two dotted-quarter chords a bar: C3 E3 G3 (bars 5-6), D3 G3 B3 (bar 7), and holds C3 E3 G3 under the final 'dream.'

score_note: Catalog-relative whole-piece 0–10 score from pianoflow/tools/score_pieces.py after Row, Row, Row Your Boat and Itsy Bitsy Spider were added. Raw = w1 + 0.35·w2 + 0.2·w3 + min(0.1·sum(rest), 2.0) on tagged technique weights; score = 0.3 + (raw − min_raw)/(max_raw − min_raw)·9.6. Basic chords and inversions appear in the full-rung instance scores but are below the tag thresholds (0.5 × weight), so they are not tagged on the whole piece. Adding a piece can shift other catalog scores (the formula is catalog-relative); these two did not move the catalog minimum or maximum, so no existing score changed.
